subject: Linguistics
title: Age and Language
description: A 60-second lesson on Age and Language.

hook.text: Every generation invents new slang—and every older generation complains about it.

buildup.text: Apparent-time studies compare age groups to track language change in progress.

discovery.text: Young speakers typically lead sound changes—older speakers preserve conservative features.

twist.text: Some features are 'age-graded'—teens use them, then abandon them as adults. The change is an illusion.

climax.text: Real-time studies track the same speakers over decades to confirm whether change is genuine.

punchline.text: Young voices drive language forward—every generation.

quiz.question: What are apparent-time studies?
options: Comparing age groups to track language change
